claim: Zebrafish have dark stripes of black melanophores with light interstripes of yellow-orange xanthophores and iridescent iridophores.
source: Zebrafish have dark stripes of black melanophores with light interstripes of yellow-orange xanthophores and iridescent iridophores (Figure 1A), all of which are derived from the neural crest, either directly, or through stem cell intermediates (Budi et al., 2011; Dooley et al., 2013; Mahalwar et al., 2014; McMenamin et al., 2014; Singh et al., 2014).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 1A showing zebrafish pigment pattern; supported by multiple citations.

claim: All zebrafish pigment cells (melanophores, xanthophores, and iridophores) are derived from the neural crest, either directly or through stem cell intermediates.
source: Zebrafish have dark stripes of black melanophores with light interstripes of yellow-orange xanthophores and iridescent iridophores (Figure 1A), all of which are derived from the neural crest, either directly, or through stem cell intermediates (Budi et al., 2011; Dooley et al., 2013; Mahalwar et al., 2014; McMenamin et al., 2014; Singh et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Iridophores differentiate in the prospective interstripe and specify the positions and orientations of melanophore stripes.
source: Iridophores differentiate in the prospective interstripe, and specify the positions and orientations of melanophore stripes (Frohnhofer et al., 2013; Patterson and Parichy, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Iridophores promote the differentiation of xanthophores in the interstripe by expressing Colony stimulating factor-1 (Csf1).
source: Iridophores also promote the differentiation of xanthophores in the interstripe by expressing Colony stimulating factor-1 (Csf1)(Patterson and Parichy, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Interactions between cells of melanophore and xanthophore lineages are required during stripe consolidation.
source: Subsequently, interactions between cells of melanophore and xanthophore lineages are required during a period of stripe consolidation, in which some melanophores initially in the interstripe join the stripes, and, simultaneously, the stripe borders become increasingly organized (Parichy et al., 2000; Maderspacher and Nusslein-Volhard, 2003; Parichy and Turner, 2003a, 2003b; Quigley et al., 2005; Takahashi and Kondo, 2008).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: During stripe consolidation, some melanophores initially in the interstripe join the stripes and stripe borders become increasingly organized.
source: Subsequently, interactions between cells of melanophore and xanthophore lineages are required during a period of stripe consolidation, in which some melanophores initially in the interstripe join the stripes, and, simultaneously, the stripe borders become increasingly organized (Parichy et al., 2000; Maderspacher and Nusslein-Volhard, 2003; Parichy and Turner, 2003a, 2003b; Quigley et al., 2005; Takahashi and Kondo, 2008).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Pearl danio has a nearly uniform pattern of fewer melanophores, more xanthophores and an intermingling of all three pigment cell classes.
source: Interesting in this context is pearl danio, D. albolineatus, which has a nearly uniform pattern of fewer melanophores, more xanthophores and an intermingling of all three pigment cell classes (Figure 1A) (Quigley et al., 2005; Mills et al., 2007; Patterson et al., 2014; McCluskey and Postlethwait, 2015).
evidence: Directly stated in text, supported by Figure 1A showing pearl danio pattern, and multiple citations.

claim: Cells of the xanthophore lineage marked by aox5 expression exhibited long, fast projections with distinctive membraneous vesicles at their tips in zebrafish.
source: In zebrafish, cells of the xanthophore lineage, marked by expression of aldehyde oxidase 5 (aox5; formerly, aox3) (Parichy et al., 2000; McMenamin et al., 2014), exhibited long, fast projections with distinctive, membraneous vesicles at their tips; vesicles were often left behind when the projection carrying them retracted or fragmented (Figure 1B,E; Video 1).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 1B,E and Video 1 showing projections.

claim: Vesicles were often left behind when projections retracted or fragmented.
source: In zebrafish, cells of the xanthophore lineage, marked by expression of aldehyde oxidase 5 (aox5; formerly, aox3) (Parichy et al., 2000; McMenamin et al., 2014), exhibited long, fast projections with distinctive, membraneous vesicles at their tips; vesicles were often left behind when the projection carrying them retracted or fragmented (Figure 1B,E; Video 1).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 1E and Video 1.

claim: Projections by aox5+ cells were especially frequent at early stages of stripe formation (7–8 SSL).
source: Such projections were especially frequent at early stages of stripe formation (7–8 SSL; Figure 1C-left; Figure 1—figure supplement 1) (Parichy and Turner, 2003b; Parichy et al., 2009; Patterson and Parichy, 2013) and individual cells could extend several projections over 18 hr of time-lapse imaging (Figure 1C-right).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 1C-left and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Individual aox5+ cells could extend several projections over 18 hr of time-lapse imaging.
source: Such projections were especially frequent at early stages of stripe formation (7–8 SSL; Figure 1C-left; Figure 1—figure supplement 1) (Parichy and Turner, 2003b; Parichy et al., 2009; Patterson and Parichy, 2013) and individual cells could extend several projections over 18 hr of time-lapse imaging (Figure 1C-right).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 1C-right.

claim: Projections reached as far as 5–6 cell diameters.
source: Projections reached as far as 5–6 cell diameters and extended and retracted quickly (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 1D,E.

claim: Projections extended and retracted quickly.
source: Projections reached as far as 5–6 cell diameters and extended and retracted quickly (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 1D,E.

claim: Incidences of projection formation were not markedly altered in mutants lacking melanophores or iridophores.
source: Incidences of projection formation were not markedly altered in mutants lacking melanophores or iridophores, or in transgenic fish having supernumerary melanophores (Figure 1—figure supplement 2; Video 2).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Video 2.

claim: Incidences of projection formation were not markedly altered in transgenic fish having supernumerary melanophores.
source: Incidences of projection formation were not markedly altered in mutants lacking melanophores or iridophores, or in transgenic fish having supernumerary melanophores (Figure 1—figure supplement 2; Video 2).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Video 2.

claim: Fast projections were extended only rarely by aox5+ cells of pearl danio.
source: By contrast, fast projections were extended only rarely by aox5+ cells of pearl danio (Figure 1C,E; Figure 1—figure supplement 1 Video 1).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 1C,E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, and Video 1.

claim: Fast projections were rare among melanophores of both zebrafish and pearl danio species.
source: Likewise, fast projections were rare among melanophores of both species, marked by expression of tyrosinase related protein 1b (tyrp1b; Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Video 3) and were not observed for iridophores, marked by purine nucleoside phosphorylase 4a (pnp4a; Video 4) (Lang et al., 2009; Curran et al., 2010; McMenamin et al., 2014).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and Video 3.

claim: Fast projections were not observed for iridophores.
source: Likewise, fast projections were rare among melanophores of both species, marked by expression of tyrosinase related protein 1b (tyrp1b; Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Video 3) and were not observed for iridophores, marked by purine nucleoside phosphorylase 4a (pnp4a; Video 4) (Lang et al., 2009; Curran et al., 2010; McMenamin et al., 2014).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Video 4.

claim: Fast projections of pigment cells contained F-actin.
source: Similar to cytonemes, fast pigment cell projections contained F-actin, as evidenced by labeling with fluorescent reporters fused to the calponin homology domain of utrophin (UtrCH) as well as LifeAct (Burkel et al., 2007; Riedl et al., 2008; Sanders et al., 2013) (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 2A,B showing F-actin labeling; supported by citations.

claim: Fast projections had highly meandering trajectories.
source: In contrast to cytonemes, however, fast projections had highly meandering trajectories and the vesicles associated with them had diameters of 1.7 ± 0.1 µm (mean ± SE, n=22), considerably larger than the 30–200 nm exosome-like particles trafficked within cytonemes (Bischoff et al., 2013; Sanders et al., 2013; Gradilla et al., 2014).
evidence: Directly stated in text with comparison to cytonemes; supported by citations.

claim: Vesicles associated with fast projections had diameters of 1.7 ± 0.1 µm (mean ± SE, n=22).
source: In contrast to cytonemes, however, fast projections had highly meandering trajectories and the vesicles associated with them had diameters of 1.7 ± 0.1 µm (mean ± SE, n=22), considerably larger than the 30–200 nm exosome-like particles trafficked within cytonemes (Bischoff et al., 2013; Sanders et al., 2013; Gradilla et al., 2014).
evidence: Directly stated in text with quantitative measurement.

claim: Vesicles associated with fast projections are considerably larger than the 30–200 nm exosome-like particles trafficked within cytonemes.
source: In contrast to cytonemes, however, fast projections had highly meandering trajectories and the vesicles associated with them had diameters of 1.7 ± 0.1 µm (mean ± SE, n=22), considerably larger than the 30–200 nm exosome-like particles trafficked within cytonemes (Bischoff et al., 2013; Sanders et al., 2013; Gradilla et al., 2014).
evidence: Directly stated in text with comparison to cytonemes; supported by citations.

claim: Filaments of fast projections contained tubulin.
source: Also unlike cytonemes, filaments of fast projections contained tubulin, as indicated by localization of an alpha tubulin fusion protein; such labeling was present in some but not all projection-associated vesicles (Figure 2C).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 2C showing tubulin labeling.

claim: Tubulin labeling was present in some but not all projection-associated vesicles.
source: Also unlike cytonemes, filaments of fast projections contained tubulin, as indicated by localization of an alpha tubulin fusion protein; such labeling was present in some but not all projection-associated vesicles (Figure 2C).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 2C.

claim: Fast projections and vesicles exhibited transient accumulations of microtubule plus-end binding protein EB3.
source: Suggesting active microtubule assembly, fast projections and vesicles also exhibited transient accumulations of microtubule plus-end binding protein EB3 (Figure 2D; Video 5).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 2D and Video 5.

claim: The transient accumulations of EB3 suggest active microtubule assembly in fast projections.
source: Suggesting active microtubule assembly, fast projections and vesicles also exhibited transient accumulations of microtubule plus-end binding protein EB3 (Figure 2D; Video 5).
evidence: Directly stated in text as an interpretation of EB3 accumulation data.

claim: Fast projections were termed 'airinemes' based on their distinctive morphology, cytoskeletal composition, and function.
source: Given their distinctive morphology and cytoskeletal composition, as well as their function (below), we termed these fast projections 'airinemes,' for Iris, who—fleet as the wind on golden wings—delivered messages for the gods (Homer, ~8th cent. BCE), as well as for Sir George Biddell Airy, who described limits on optical resolution (Cox, 2012).
evidence: Directly stated in text with explanation of naming rationale; supported by citation.

claim: aox5+ cells occur in the prospective interstripe where they differentiate as xanthophores beginning around 6.5 SSL.
source: In zebrafish, aox5+ cells occur in the prospective interstripe, where they differentiate as xanthophores [beginning ~6.5 SSL (Parichy et al., 2009; Patterson and Parichy, 2013)].
evidence: Directly stated in text with stage specification; supported by citations.

claim: aox5+ cells occur at lower densities in developing and completed stripes where they remain unpigmented or lightly pigmented.
source: Yet, aox5+ cells also occur at lower densities in developing and completed stripes, where they remain unpigmented or lightly pigmented (Figure 3A); we refer to these incompletely differentiated cells as xanthoblasts (McMenamin et al., 2014).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 3A; supported by citation.

claim: Incompletely differentiated aox5+ cells in stripes are referred to as xanthoblasts.
source: Yet, aox5+ cells also occur at lower densities in developing and completed stripes, where they remain unpigmented or lightly pigmented (Figure 3A); we refer to these incompletely differentiated cells as xanthoblasts (McMenamin et al., 2014).
evidence: Directly stated in text as a definition; supported by citation.

claim: aox5+ cells within stripe regions (presumptive xanthoblasts) were more likely to extend airinemes than cells within the developing interstripe (presumptive xanthophores).
source: We found that cells within stripe regions, presumptive xanthoblasts, were more likely to extend airinemes than were cells within the developing interstripe, presumptive xanthophores (Figure 3B).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 3B showing quantitative comparison.

claim: Unpigmented xanthoblasts, but not pigmented xanthophores, had membrane blebs from which airinemes originated.
source: Inspection of aox5+ cells at high resolution further revealed that unpigmented xanthoblasts, but not pigmented xanthophores, had membrane blebs from which airinemes originated (Figure 3C; Videos 6, 7).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 3C and Videos 6, 7.

claim: aox5+ cells arrested as xanthoblasts (TH–) produced more airinemes than aox5+ cells forced to differentiate as xanthophores (TH++).
source: We found that aox5+ cells arrested as xanthoblasts (TH–) produced more airinemes than aox5+ cells forced to differentiate as xanthophores (TH++; Figure 3D; Video 8).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 3D and Video 8 showing experimental manipulation.

claim: Airineme production is differentiation-state specific within the xanthophore lineage.
source: These findings are consistent with the interpretation that airineme production is differentiation-state specific within the xanthophore lineage (and see below)
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the TH manipulation experiments.

claim: Airineme production was curtailed by acute treatment with the myosin II inhibitor blebbistatin.
source: Consistent with actin and tubulin cytoskeletal dependencies, airineme production was curtailed by acute treatment with the myosin II inhibitor blebbistatin (Kovacs et al., 2004) and the microtubule polymerization inhibitor nocodazole (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), although longer term whole-fish treatments were lethal.
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1A; supported by citation.

claim: Airineme production was curtailed by acute treatment with the microtubule polymerization inhibitor nocodazole.
source: Consistent with actin and tubulin cytoskeletal dependencies, airineme production was curtailed by acute treatment with the myosin II inhibitor blebbistatin (Kovacs et al., 2004) and the microtubule polymerization inhibitor nocodazole (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), although longer term whole-fish treatments were lethal.
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Low levels of the Cdc42 small GTPase inhibitor ML141 inhibited airineme production while allowing for extended whole-fish treatments.
source: By contrast, low levels of the Cdc42 small GTPase inhibitor ML141 (Surviladze et al., 2010) inhibited airineme production (Video 9) while allowing for extended whole-fish treatments.
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Video 9; supported by citation.

claim: In larvae treated with ML141 through adult pigment pattern formation, melanophores occurred ectopically within the interstripe.
source: In larvae treated with ML141 through adult pigment pattern formation, melanophores occurred ectopically within the interstripe (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Extended, low-level induction of dnCdc42 in aox5+ cells inhibited airineme production.
source: We found that extended, low-level induction of dnCdc42 in aox5+ cells inhibited airineme production (Figure 4A; Video 10) without significantly affecting the production of short filopodia, lamellipodia-like protrusive activities, the numbers of differentiated xanthophores or melanophores, or the distributions of aox5+ cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B–F).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4A and Video 10.

claim: dnCdc42 induction in aox5+ cells did not significantly affect the production of short filopodia, lamellipodia-like protrusive activities, the numbers of differentiated xanthophores or melanophores, or the distributions of aox5+ cells.
source: We found that extended, low-level induction of dnCdc42 in aox5+ cells inhibited airineme production (Figure 4A; Video 10) without significantly affecting the production of short filopodia, lamellipodia-like protrusive activities, the numbers of differentiated xanthophores or melanophores, or the distributions of aox5+ cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B–F).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 2B–F.

claim: In aox5:Tet:dnCdc42 fish inhibited for airineme production, melanophores persisted ectopically in the interstripe.
source: Yet, in aox5:Tet:dnCdc42 fish inhibited for airineme production, melanophores persisted ectopically in the interstripe (Figure 4B), as for whole fish treated with ML141.
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4B.

claim: Brownish embryonic melanophores had translocated to the edges of adult stripes in wild-type controls.
source: In wild-type controls, these brownish embryonic melanophores had translocated to the edges of adult stripes, whereas in aox5:Tet:dnCdc42-expressing fish these melanophores remained in the interstripe (insets, Figure 4B).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4B insets.

claim: In aox5:Tet:dnCdc42-expressing fish, brownish embryonic melanophores remained in the interstripe.
source: In wild-type controls, these brownish embryonic melanophores had translocated to the edges of adult stripes, whereas in aox5:Tet:dnCdc42-expressing fish these melanophores remained in the interstripe (insets, Figure 4B).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4B insets.

claim: Frequent, prolonged stabilization of aox5+ airinemes on melanophores was observed.
source: In these larvae we observed frequent, prolonged stabilization of aox5+ airinemes on melanophores (Figure 4c,d-left; Video 11).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4c,d-left and Video 11.

claim: Airinemes retracted rapidly after contacting aox5+ cells, indicating target specificity.
source: In contrast, airinemes retracted rapidly after contacting aox5+ cells (Figure 4d-left), indicating target specificity.
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4d-left.

claim: Airinemes often stabilized on persisting embryonic melanophores (Me) and newly differentiating, still migratory adult melanophores (Mn), but rarely on previously differentiated adult melanophores (Mp).
source: Airinemes often stabilized on Me and newly differentiating, still migratory adult melanophores (Mn), but rarely on previously differentiated adult melanophores (Mp) (Figure 4E; Figure 4—figure supplement 3; Videos 11, 12).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 3, and Videos 11, 12.

claim: Airineme-delivered vesicles often remained on melanophores long after the airineme itself.
source: Moreover, airineme-delivered vesicles often remained on melanophores long after the airineme itself (Figure 4G; Video 13).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4G and Video 13.

claim: In some instances, vesicles were transferred without evident airinemes.
source: In some instances, vesicles were transferred without evident airinemes (Video 14), a behavior that was also abrogated by dnCdc42.
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Video 14.

claim: Vesicle transfer without evident airinemes was abrogated by dnCdc42.
source: In some instances, vesicles were transferred without evident airinemes (Video 14), a behavior that was also abrogated by dnCdc42.
evidence: Directly stated in text.

claim: Airinemes in spotted connexin41.8 (cx41.8; leopard) mutants were later-appearing and more promiscuous than in wild-type zebrafish.
source: As compared to wild-type zebrafish, we found that airinemes in spotted connexin41.8 (cx41.8; leopard) mutants (Maderspacher and Nusslein-Volhard, 2003; Watanabe et al., 2006) were later-appearing and more promiscuous, stabilizing as extensively on aox5+ cells as on melanophores (Figure 4D-right, 4F; Figure 4—figure supplement 4A,B; Video 15).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4D-right, 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 4A,B, and Video 15; supported by citations.

claim: Airinemes in cx41.8 mutants stabilized as extensively on aox5+ cells as on melanophores.
source: As compared to wild-type zebrafish, we found that airinemes in spotted connexin41.8 (cx41.8; leopard) mutants (Maderspacher and Nusslein-Volhard, 2003; Watanabe et al., 2006) were later-appearing and more promiscuous, stabilizing as extensively on aox5+ cells as on melanophores (Figure 4D-right, 4F; Figure 4—figure supplement 4A,B; Video 15).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4D-right, 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 4A,B, and Video 15.

claim: The rare airinemes of pearl danio stabilized on xanthophores.
source: Interestingly, the rare airinemes of pearl danio also stabilized on xanthophores though inspection cx41.8 sequence and expression did not reveal gross differences between zebrafish and pearl (Figure 4D-right; Video 16; and data not shown).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 4D-right and Video 16.

claim: Inspection of cx41.8 sequence and expression did not reveal gross differences between zebrafish and pearl danio.
source: Interestingly, the rare airinemes of pearl danio also stabilized on xanthophores though inspection cx41.8 sequence and expression did not reveal gross differences between zebrafish and pearl (Figure 4D-right; Video 16; and data not shown).
evidence: Directly stated in text.

claim: Airinemes extended by aox5+ xanthoblasts in prospective stripe regions contact melanophores still in the interstripe and promote their clearance during stripe consolidation in wild-type zebrafish.
source: Together these results suggest that, in wild-type zebrafish, airinemes extended by aox5+ xanthoblasts in prospective stripe regions contact melanophores still in the interstripe and promote their clearance during stripe consolidation, and that specificity of airineme targeting is genetically (and evolutionarily) labile.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Specificity of airineme targeting is genetically and evolutionarily labile.
source: Together these results suggest that, in wild-type zebrafish, airinemes extended by aox5+ xanthoblasts in prospective stripe regions contact melanophores still in the interstripe and promote their clearance during stripe consolidation, and that specificity of airineme targeting is genetically (and evolutionarily) labile.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the mutant and interspecific comparison results.

claim: In zebrafish, xanthophores express Delta genes whereas melanophores express Notch genes.
source: In zebrafish as well as pearl danio, xanthophores express Delta genes whereas melanophores express Notch genes (Hamada et al., 2014) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1A; supported by citation.

claim: In pearl danio, xanthophores express Delta genes whereas melanophores express Notch genes.
source: In zebrafish as well as pearl danio, xanthophores express Delta genes whereas melanophores express Notch genes (Hamada et al., 2014) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1A; supported by citation.

claim: Expressing the constitutively active Notch1a intracellular domain in melanophores resulted in stripes that were significantly broader than in wild type.
source: Consistent with a role for Notch in promoting melanophore migration, we found that expressing the constitutively active Notch1a intracellular domain in melanophores, using a promoter derived from the microphthalmia a (mitfa) gene (Lister et al., 1999), resulted in stripes that were significantly broader than in wild type (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1B; supported by citation.

claim: DlC-mCherry was present in airineme vesicles.
source: We recombineered a 109 kb BAC containing zebrafish dlc coding sequence and regulatory elements to generate an mCherry fusion that was functional in rescuing dlc knockdown phenotypes; static and time-lapse imaging confirmed that DlC-mCherry was present in airineme vesicles (Figure 5A; Video 17).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5A and Video 17.

claim: Frequencies of Tp1+ Notch-responding melanophores were reduced in the absence of aox5+ cells (csf1ra mutants).
source: To test whether this level of activity reflected signaling from cells of the xanthophore lineage, we examined colony stimulating factor-1 receptor a (csf1ra) homozygous mutants, which lack virtually all xanthophores and xanthoblasts (Parichy et al., 2000; Patterson and Parichy, 2013) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), and found a marked reduction in the incidence of Tp1+ melanophores compared to wild-type siblings.
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2; supported by citations.

claim: Airineme-inhibited fish expressing aox5:Tet:dnCdc42 showed a significant reduction in Tp1+ melanophores compared to dd-treated but non-transgenic siblings.
source: To test for an airineme-dependence of such signaling, we examined airineme-inhibited fish expressing aox5:Tet:dnCdc42 and found a significant reduction in Tp1+ melanophores compared to dd-treated but non-transgenic siblings (Figure 5B).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: Global pharmacological inhibition of Notch signaling resulted in disruptions to melanophore stripe consolidation.
source: Indeed, global pharmacological inhibition of Notch signaling resulted in disruptions to melanophore stripe consolidation (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 3A.

claim: mitfa:Tet:dnSu(H) reduced expression of Notch target gene her6.
source: mitfa:Tet:dnSu(H) reduced expression of Notch target gene her6 but did not affect total numbers of melanophores or xanthophores that differentiated (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B–D).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 3B–D.

claim: mitfa:Tet:dnSu(H) did not affect total numbers of melanophores or xanthophores that differentiated.
source: mitfa:Tet:dnSu(H) reduced expression of Notch target gene her6 but did not affect total numbers of melanophores or xanthophores that differentiated (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B–D).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 3B–D.

claim: Similar to effects of dnCdc42-airineme inhibition, melanophores persisted ectopically in the interstripe in mitfa:Tet:dnSu(H) fish.
source: Similar to effects of dnCdc42-airineme inhibition, however, melanophores persisted ectopically in the interstripe (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5C,D.

claim: When aox5:Tet:dnCdc42 and mitfa:Tet:dnSu(H) transgenes were combined at very low induction levels, ectopic melanophores persisted in the interstripe.
source: Accordingly, we induced transgenes at very low levels that were insufficient to cause a phenotype when transgenes were present individually. When transgenes were combined, however, ectopic melanophores persisted in the interstripe (Figure 5E).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5E.

claim: Fish induced to express aox5:Tet:dnCdc42 at standard levels had significantly fewer ectopic melanophores when transgenic simultaneously for mitfa:NICD1a.
source: Conversely, fish induced to express aox5:Tet:dnCdc42 at standard levels had significantly fewer ectopic melanophores when transgenic simultaneously for mitfa:NICD1a (mean ± SE melanophores: dnCdc42, 26.4 ± 1.1; dnCdc42 with NICD1a, 9.2 ± 1.5; F1,8=84.5, p<0.001).
evidence: Directly stated in text with quantitative data.

claim: Melanophores of fish heterozygous for a kita null allele were sensitized to very low level induction of mitfa:Tet:dnSu(H) and aox5:Tet:dnCdc42.
source: Consistent with this idea, we found that melanophores of fish heterozygous for a kita null allele were sensitized to very low level induction of mitfa:Tet:dnSu(H) and aox5:Tet:dnCdc42 (Figure 5—figure supplement 5A,B).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 5A,B.

claim: Abundances of kita transcript were moderately reduced in melanophores in the absence of xanthophores.
source: Abundances of kita transcript were also moderately reduced in melanophores, both in the absence of xanthophores and after inducing mitfa:Tet:dnSu(H) or aox5:Tet:dnCdc42 transgenes (Figure 5—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 5C.

claim: Abundances of kita transcript were moderately reduced in melanophores after inducing mitfa:Tet:dnSu(H) or aox5:Tet:dnCdc42 transgenes.
source: Abundances of kita transcript were also moderately reduced in melanophores, both in the absence of xanthophores and after inducing mitfa:Tet:dnSu(H) or aox5:Tet:dnCdc42 transgenes (Figure 5—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 5C.

claim: Melanophores of pearl danio exhibited reductions in Notch-responsive her6 and kita transcripts.
source: Indeed, melanophores of pearl danio, which migrate less than zebrafish (Quigley et al., 2005), exhibited similar reductions in Notch-responsive her6 and kita transcripts (Figure 5—figure supplement 5D).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 5D; supported by citation.

claim: aox5+ airinemes extended by xanthoblasts promote Notch signaling and Kita-dependent melanophore rearrangements during stripe consolidation in zebrafish.
source: These observations support a model in which aox5+ airinemes extended by xanthoblasts promote Notch signaling and Kita-dependent melanophore rearrangements during stripe consolidation in zebrafish.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Experimental arrest of aox5+ cell differentiation in pearl danio (TH–) increased airineme production, albeit not to levels observed in zebrafish.
source: Consistent with this idea, experimental arrest of aox5+ cell differentiation in pearl danio (TH–) increased airineme production, albeit not to levels observed in zebrafish (Figure 6A-left).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 6A-left.

claim: Zebrafish aox5+ cells in pearl danio hosts extended airinemes at reduced frequencies, similar to that of pearl danio aox5+ cells.
source: Zebrafish aox5+ cells in pearl danio hosts extended airinemes at reduced frequencies, similar to that of pearl danio aox5+ cells (Figure 6A-right; Video 18).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 6A-right and Video 18.

claim: Species differences in airineme production are non-autonomous to the xanthophore lineage.
source: We interpret this observation, as well as aox5+ cell behaviors in reciprocal transplants, and adult pigment patterns of chimeras (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), as indicating species differences that are non-autonomous to the xanthophore lineage.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of transplantation experiments; supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Overexpression of Csf1 in zebrafish resulted in a 22% reduction in airineme frequency within 24 hr.
source: Consistent with this idea, overexpression of Csf1 in zebrafish resulted in a 22% reduction in airineme frequency within 24 hr and an 86% reduction after complete xanthophore differentiation, as in pearl (Figure 6A-right; Video 19).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 6A-right and Video 19.

claim: Overexpression of Csf1 in zebrafish resulted in an 86% reduction in airineme frequency after complete xanthophore differentiation.
source: Consistent with this idea, overexpression of Csf1 in zebrafish resulted in a 22% reduction in airineme frequency within 24 hr and an 86% reduction after complete xanthophore differentiation, as in pearl (Figure 6A-right; Video 19).
evidence: Directly stated in text and supported by Figure 6A-right and Video 19.

claim: Infrequent airineme extension in pearl danio arises at least in part from evolutionary changes in factors extrinsic to the xanthophore lineage.
source: Together, these results support the interpretation that infrequent airineme extension, as well as pattern differences in pearl danio as compared to zebrafish, arise at least in part from evolutionary changes in factors extrinsic to the xanthophore lineage, and identify Csf1 as an especially good candidate for mediating these effects.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the transplantation and Csf1 manipulation experiments.

claim: Csf1 is an especially good candidate for mediating pattern differences between zebrafish and pearl danio.
source: Together, these results support the interpretation that infrequent airineme extension, as well as pattern differences in pearl danio as compared to zebrafish, arise at least in part from evolutionary changes in factors extrinsic to the xanthophore lineage, and identify Csf1 as an especially good candidate for mediating these effects.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Airinemes are a novel mode of long distance cellular communication.
source: More generally, our approaches have identified a novel mode of long distance cellular communication, and provide fresh insights into evolutionary changes in morphogenesis during pigment pattern development.
evidence: Stated as a summary conclusion of the study.

claim: Airinemes are considerably longer than typical (<10 µm) filopodia.
source: Fast projections were considerably longer than typical (<10 µm) filopodia, that lacked vesicles (e.g., Figure 1—figure supplement 3D; and below).
evidence: Directly stated in text with comparison to filopodia; supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 3D.

claim: Typical filopodia lack vesicles.
source: Fast projections were considerably longer than typical (<10 µm) filopodia, that lacked vesicles (e.g., Figure 1—figure supplement 3D; and below).
evidence: Directly stated in text; supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 3D.

claim: Enhanced Csf1 expression drives precocious, widespread xanthophore differentiation in pearl danio.
source: Finally, interspecific transplants and transgenic manipulations in this study provide new insights into the nearly uniform pattern of pearl danio, and together suggest a model in which enhanced Csf1 expression drives precocious, widespread xanthophore differentiation, limiting positional information available to melanophores (Patterson et al., 2014), as well as airineme production and the potential for melanophore migration and stripe consolidation (Figure 6C—right).
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the experimental results; supported by Figure 6C and citation.

claim: Enhanced Csf1 expression in pearl danio limits positional information available to melanophores.
source: Finally, interspecific transplants and transgenic manipulations in this study provide new insights into the nearly uniform pattern of pearl danio, and together suggest a model in which enhanced Csf1 expression drives precocious, widespread xanthophore differentiation, limiting positional information available to melanophores (Patterson et al., 2014), as well as airineme production and the potential for melanophore migration and stripe consolidation (Figure 6C—right).
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the experimental results; supported by Figure 6C and citation.

claim: Differentiated xanthophores repel melanophores during normal development.
source: Differentiated xanthophores repel melanophores (X⊣M) during normal development (Nakamasu et al., 2009) and are capable of repressing iridophore organization (X⊣I) [for details, see: (Patterson et al., 2014)].
evidence: Directly stated in text; supported by citations.

claim: Differentiated xanthophores are capable of repressing iridophore organization.
source: Differentiated xanthophores repel melanophores (X⊣M) during normal development (Nakamasu et al., 2009) and are capable of repressing iridophore organization (X⊣I) [for details, see: (Patterson et al., 2014)].
evidence: Directly stated in text; supported by citation.

claim: In pearl danio, Csf1 is expressed at elevated levels by cells other than iridophores.
source: In pearl danio, Csf1 is expressed at elevated levels by cells other than iridophores and this drives earlier and broader xanthophore differentiation than in zebrafish (Patterson et al., 2014).
evidence: Directly stated in text; supported by citation.

claim: Elevated Csf1 expression in pearl danio drives earlier and broader xanthophore differentiation than in zebrafish.
source: In pearl danio, Csf1 is expressed at elevated levels by cells other than iridophores and this drives earlier and broader xanthophore differentiation than in zebrafish (Patterson et al., 2014).
evidence: Directly stated in text; supported by citation.

claim: Iridophores have attractive and repulsive effects on melanophores.
source: In addition to xanthoblast–melanophore interactions, iridophores have attractive and repulsive effects on melanophores (I→M; I⊣M) (Frohnhofer et al., 2013; Patterson and Parichy, 2013) and express Csf1, promoting the differentiation of xanthophores (Xb→X) at the interstripe (Patterson and Parichy, 2013).
evidence: Directly stated in text; supported by citations.
